title: Label rollback decision scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal notebook for deciding when to rollback a recent labeling guideline change or bulk re-label job.
- Capture heuristics, edge examples, and an operational checklist to hand to ops/SEs.

Context / impetus:
- We shipped relax-date-boundary rule last week (PR 312). Some downstream evals show precision drop on product-title extraction for ecom dataset.
- Need fast way to decide: revert labeling change, patch rules, or accept drift and mark as model-expected.

Key constraints (informal):
- Rollbacks are disruptive (cost, rework, versioning). Prefer targeted fixes unless clear systemic regression.
- If customer-facing metrics degrade >2% absolute F1 on gold prompts, escalate.
- If annotator confusion >30% disagreement on adjudication sample, lean rollback.

Quick triage checklist (first 24h):
1) Reproduce regression on a stable eval set (snapshot before guideline change).
   - Run pre-change snapshot vs post-change on 3 slices: head (top 10k), mid (10k-100k), tail (100k+).
2) Sample 100 errors where label differs; annotate locally with 2 validators.
3) Check whether error cluster maps to a single rule change (e.g., date-boundary) or multiple unrelated edits.
4) Check linked artifacts: PR comments, annotator threads, slack threads (#labeling).
5) If failure is concentrated in a single semantic bucket AND manual review consensus >= 70% that pre-change was correct -> consider rollback.

Heuristic scoring (ad hoc, 0-10):
- Eval delta severity: (abs delta F1) * 5 -> up to 5 points.
- Coverage: % of affected examples in production traffic (est) / 20 -> up to 5 points.
- Annotator consensus (inverted): (1 - consensus) * 5 -> penalize low consensus when deciding rollback.
- If score >=7 => immediate rollback candidate; 4-6 => targeted patch + canary; <4 => observe.

Example cases (notes from sampling):
A) Product title trimming change (observed):
- Symptom: titles with trailing SKU-like tokens now get shorter labels, model output missing brand tag.
- Manual check (n=50): 36 examples prefer pre-change labels -> consensus 72%.
- Impact on eval F1: -3.4 absolute.
- Traffic coverage: ~0.8% of labelable items.
- Decision: consider rollback (score ~7.1).

B) Abbreviation expansion (relaxed):
- Symptom: we expanded Abbrev -> full form aggressively. Some ambiguous abbreviations got incorrect expansions.
- Manual check (n=80): low consensus (40%) split cases across two valid interpretations.
- Eval delta: -0.6 absolute.
- Decision: do NOT rollback; create exception rules for high-ambiguity contexts and update prompts.

C) Date boundary rule (edge):
- Symptom: over-eager merging of date ranges into single token.
- Manual check (n=60): 18 prefer pre-change (30% consensus), 42 prefer post-change (70%).
- Eval delta: -1.1 absolute on date extraction slice, but downstream NER downstream unaffected.
- Decision: observe, tweak kernels (adjust lookback) and rescore. No rollback.

Rollback procedure (operational, quick):
1) Create rollback PR reverting labeling rules files and tagging dataset snapshot to revert-YYYYMMDD.
2) Post a short note to #labeling + #ml-ops with reason, metrics, and rollback tag.
3) Small canary: reprocess 10k examples from production tail and run model inference in isolated workspace. Compare.
4) If canary confirms improvement and low side-effects, schedule full reprocess during off-peak with ops.
5) Post-mortem: short doc with what went wrong, how to avoid, owners, and new gating checklist.

Rollforward alternatives (if not rolling back):
- Patch: add narrowly scoped exception rules.
- Adjudication: add contested examples to adjudication queue and update training only after consensus.
- Model-level mitigation: add prompt/decoder constraints to re-weight labels.

Metrics to capture for decision record:
- Baseline F1 (pre-change) and post-change F1 on stable gold set.
- Absolute deltas by slice (head/mid/tail).
- Annotator consensus % on sampled disagreements.
- Estimated traffic coverage and revenue-impact proxy (if applicable).
- Time-to-fix estimate and reprocessing cost estimate.

Templates (quick copy):
- Slack blurb: "Heads-up: rolling back rule X (PR 312) due to -3.4 F1 on product-title slice. Canary shows 1.8% lift. Rolling back if no objections by EOD. Details: <link to PR + sample>."
- Rollback PR title: "revert(rule-date-boundary): revert change from PR 312 — causes product-title regressions"

Open questions / TODOs:
- How long to wait observing after a non-rollback decision? 2 weeks? 1 release cycle? Need explicit policy.
- Automate sampling: build pipeline to auto-sample 200 disagreements after each large labeling push. (JIRA-LAB-598)
- Add a short checkbox in labeling workflows: "impact-risk" field to capture likely production surface area before landing changes.
- Can we instrument quick A/B model runs without full reprocess to estimate end-user impact faster?

Notes to self:
- Keep the scoring scheme simple and explainable to PMs.
- Favor minimal, reversible changes in future rule updates.
- When in doubt, push to canary + targeted patch instead of full rollback.

References / links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/labeling-tool/pull/312
- Task: JIRA-LAB-598 (auto-sampling pipeline)
- Annotator thread: slack thread ts: 1678932000 (search #labeling)

Last quick checklist before acting:
- [ ] Reproduce locally on gold snapshot
- [ ] Sample 100 disagreements + 2x validators
- [ ] Compute F1 delta and traffic coverage estimate
- [ ] Draft rollback PR + slack blurb
- [ ] Run canary (10k) and check side-effects

-- end of scratchpad --
